claim: The Nix-TB clinical trial evaluated a 6 month regimen containing bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL regimen) for the treatment of tuberculosis.
source: The Nix-TB clinical trial evaluated a new 6 month regimen containing three oral drugs; bedaquiline (B), pretomanid (Pa), and linezolid (L) (BPaL regimen) for the treatment of tuberculosis (TB).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, referencing the Nix-TB clinical trial.

claim: Almost 90% of multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant TB participants were cured with the BPaL regimen in the Nix-TB trial.
source: This regimen achieved remarkable results as almost 90% of the multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant TB participants were cured but many patients also developed severe adverse events (AEs).
evidence: The abstract states this efficacy outcome from the Nix-TB trial.

claim: Many patients treated with the BPaL regimen developed severe adverse events.
source: This regimen achieved remarkable results as almost 90% of the multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant TB participants were cured but many patients also developed severe adverse events (AEs).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that severe AEs occurred.

claim: The adverse events in the BPaL regimen were associated with long-term administration of linezolid.
source: The AEs were associated with the long-term administration of the protein synthesis inhibitor linezolid.
evidence: The abstract directly attributes AEs to linezolid administration.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 is a protein synthesis inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
source: Spectinamide 1599 is also a protein synthesis inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with an excellent safety profile, but it lacks oral bioavailability.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this mechanism of action.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 has an excellent safety profile.
source: Spectinamide 1599 is also a protein synthesis inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with an excellent safety profile, but it lacks oral bioavailability.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the safety profile of spectinamide 1599.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 lacks oral bioavailability.
source: Spectinamide 1599 is also a protein synthesis inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with an excellent safety profile, but it lacks oral bioavailability.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this limitation.

claim: Inhaled spectinamide 1599 combined with bedaquiline and pretomanid (BPaS regimen) has similar efficacy to the BPaL regimen.
source: Here, we propose to replace L in the BPaL regimen with spectinamide (S) administered via inhalation and we demonstrate that inhaled spectinamide 1599, combined with BPa ––BPaS regimen––has similar efficacy to that of the BPaL regimen while simultaneously avoiding the L-associated AEs.
evidence: The abstract states this as a main finding of the study.

claim: The BPaS regimen avoids linezolid-associated adverse events.
source: Here, we propose to replace L in the BPaL regimen with spectinamide (S) administered via inhalation and we demonstrate that inhaled spectinamide 1599, combined with BPa ––BPaS regimen––has similar efficacy to that of the BPaL regimen while simultaneously avoiding the L-associated AEs.
evidence: The abstract states this as a main finding.

claim: After 4 weeks of treatment, both BPaL and BPaS regimens promoted equivalent bactericidal effects in BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ murine TB models.
source: After 4-weeks of treatment, both regimens promoted equivalent bactericidal effects in both TB murine models.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from the study.

claim: Treatment with BPaL resulted in significant weight loss in mice.
source: However, treatment with BPaL resulted in significant weight loss and the complete blood count suggested the development of anemia.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this adverse effect.

claim: Complete blood count analysis suggested the development of anemia in mice treated with BPaL.
source: However, treatment with BPaL resulted in significant weight loss and the complete blood count suggested the development of anemia.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from CBC analysis.

claim: Weight loss and anemia effects were not observed in mice treated with BPaS.
source: These effects were not similarly observed in mice treated with BPaS.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the absence of these effects in BPaS-treated mice.

claim: BPaL and BPa, but not BPaS treatment, decreased myeloid to erythroid ratio.
source: BPaL and BPa, but not the BPaS treatment, also decreased myeloid to erythroid ratio suggesting the S in the BPaS regimen was able to recover this effect.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from bone marrow analysis.

claim: Spectinamide in the BPaS regimen was able to recover the altered myeloid to erythroid ratio effect.
source: BPaL and BPa, but not the BPaS treatment, also decreased myeloid to erythroid ratio suggesting the S in the BPaS regimen was able to recover this effect.
evidence: The abstract states this interpretation of the data.

claim: BPaL increased concentration of proinflammatory cytokines in bone marrow compared to mice receiving BPaS regimen.
source: Moreover, the BPaL also increased concentration of proinflammatory cytokines in bone marrow compared to mice receiving BPaS regimen.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from cytokine analysis.

claim: In 2021, the World Health Organization reported 10.6 million new TB cases worldwide.
source: In 2021, the World Health Organization reported 10.6 million new TB cases worldwide, and among those, 450,000 cases were also diagnosed as multidrug-resistant (MDR) or extensiverly drug-resistant (XDR) TB (Campbell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Campbell et al., 2022.

claim: Among the 10.6 million TB cases in 2021, 450,000 cases were diagnosed as multidrug-resistant or extensively drug-resistant TB.
source: In 2021, the World Health Organization reported 10.6 million new TB cases worldwide, and among those, 450,000 cases were also diagnosed as multidrug-resistant (MDR) or extensiverly drug-resistant (XDR) TB (Campbell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Treatment of MDR- and XDR-TB patients is lengthy and often poorly tolerated due to significant side effects.
source: Treatment of MDR- and XDR-TB patients is lengthy and is often poorly tolerated due to significant associated side effects (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: Preclinical studies demonstrated better efficacy of BPaL regimen for drug-sensitive TB compared to standard TB chemotherapy.
source: Preclinical studies demonstrated the better efficacy of BPaL regimen for drug-sensitive TB compared to the standard TB chemotherapy (Campbell et al., 2022; Williams et al., 2012; Tasneen et al., 2016) and thereafter, the BPaL regimen was tested in the Nix-TB clinical trial conducted in South Africa (Conradie et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to preclinical studies.

claim: The Nix-TB clinical trial was conducted in South Africa.
source: Preclinical studies demonstrated the better efficacy of BPaL regimen for drug-sensitive TB compared to the standard TB chemotherapy (Campbell et al., 2022; Williams et al., 2012; Tasneen et al., 2016) and thereafter, the BPaL regimen was tested in the Nix-TB clinical trial conducted in South Africa (Conradie et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The Nix-TB trial enrolled patients with XDR-TB and treatment-intolerant or non-responsive MDR-TB, including HIV-positive patients with a CD4 count of 50 or higher.
source: This trial enrolled patients with XDR-TB and treatment-intolerant or non-responsive MDR-TB, including HIV-positive patients with a CD4 count of 50 or higher.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the Nix-TB trial.

claim: 95 out of 107 patients were cured in the Nix-TB trial.
source: The results were remarkable as 95 out of 107 patients were cured though many patients had a high rate of treatment-associated AEs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing Nix-TB trial results.

claim: Many patients in the Nix-TB trial had a high rate of treatment-associated adverse events.
source: The results were remarkable as 95 out of 107 patients were cured though many patients had a high rate of treatment-associated AEs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Long-term administration of linezolid was likely the causative agent resulting in bone marrow myelosuppression (48%), peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis (81%), and anemia (37%) in patients treated with the BPaL regimen in the Nix-TB trial.
source: The long-term administration of linezolid (an oxazolidinone antibiotic) was likely the causative agent resulting in bone marrow myelosuppression (48%), peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis (81%), and anemia (37%) in patients treated with the BPaL regimen (Conradie et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the Nix-TB trial.

claim: The ZeNix trial adjusted the BPaL regimen to a linezolid dose of 600 mg.
source: Subsequently, the ZeNix trial adjusted the BPaL regimen to a linezolid dose of 600 mg.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: The ZeNix trial cured 84–91% of patients (9–26 weeks of therapy, respectively).
source: This trial also had remarkable results; it cured 84–91% of patients (9–26 weeks of therapy, respectively) and resulted in fewer AEs than those observed in the Nix-TB trial (Conradie et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The ZeNix trial resulted in fewer adverse events than those observed in the Nix-TB trial.
source: This trial also had remarkable results; it cured 84–91% of patients (9–26 weeks of therapy, respectively) and resulted in fewer AEs than those observed in the Nix-TB trial (Conradie et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: High doses of linezolid can lead to the development of linezolid-resistant Mtb.
source: Apart from AEs, several studies have also raised awareness of high doses of linezolid leading to the development of linezolid-resistant Mtb (TB-Alliance, 2022; Jackson, 2007; Richter et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinomycin is a broad-spectrum antibiotic used mainly for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
source: Spectinomycin, an aminocyclitol antibiotic, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic used mainly for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae (Holloway, 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Spectinomycin inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.
source: It inhibits bacterial protein synthesis (Kanchugal P and Selmer, 2020) and has an acceptable safety profile with no known ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity (Owusu et al., 2022; de Jager and van Altena, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Spectinomycin has an acceptable safety profile with no known ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
source: It inhibits bacterial protein synthesis (Kanchugal P and Selmer, 2020) and has an acceptable safety profile with no known ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity (Owusu et al., 2022; de Jager and van Altena, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The activity of spectinomycin against Mtb is very poor.
source: The activity of spectinomycin against Mtb is very poor but its structural modification led to the development of a new series of semisynthetic analogs called spectinamides (Kanchugal P and Selmer, 2020; Temrikar et al., 2023; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Structural modification of spectinomycin led to the development of spectinamides.
source: The activity of spectinomycin against Mtb is very poor but its structural modification led to the development of a new series of semisynthetic analogs called spectinamides (Kanchugal P and Selmer, 2020; Temrikar et al., 2023; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamides bind selectively with bacterial 30S ribosomes.
source: Spectinamides bind selectively with the bacterial 30 S ribosomes and importantly, unlike linezolid, they do not bind to the mitochondrial 30 S in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Unlike linezolid, spectinamides do not bind to mitochondrial 30S in mammalian cells.
source: Spectinamides bind selectively with the bacterial 30 S ribosomes and importantly, unlike linezolid, they do not bind to the mitochondrial 30 S in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Spectinamides' potent anti-tubercular activity is attributed to their ability to evade drug efflux by Rv1258c major facilitator superfamily transporter present on the surface of Mtb.
source: Spectinamides' potent anti-tubercular activity is attributed to its ability to evade drug efflux by Rv1258c major facilitator superfamily transporter present on the surface of Mtb (Liu et al., 2017; Bruhn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamides have shown excellent activity against MDR- and XDR-Mtb strains.
source: Spectinamides have shown excellent activity against MDR- and XDR-Mtb strains (Lee et al., 2014; Robertson et al., 2017) however, their poor oral availability has limited their usage to injectable forms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Poor oral availability of spectinamides has limited their usage to injectable forms.
source: Spectinamides have shown excellent activity against MDR- and XDR-Mtb strains (Lee et al., 2014; Robertson et al., 2017) however, their poor oral availability has limited their usage to injectable forms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 has demonstrated promising results in vitro and in vivo.
source: One of the lead spectinamides, 1599, has demonstrated promising results in vitro and in vivo and was shown to lack cross-resistance with existing anti-TB drugs (Lee et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2017; Bruhn et al., 2015; Robertson et al., 2017; Gonzalez-Juarrero et al., 2021; Wagh et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 lacks cross-resistance with existing anti-TB drugs.
source: One of the lead spectinamides, 1599, has demonstrated promising results in vitro and in vivo and was shown to lack cross-resistance with existing anti-TB drugs (Lee et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2017; Bruhn et al., 2015; Robertson et al., 2017; Gonzalez-Juarrero et al., 2021; Wagh et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Subcutaneously delivered spectinamide 1599 proved an effective partner agent when combined with rifampin and pyrazinamide and also with bedaquiline, pretomanid, or moxifloxacin in TB mouse efficacy models.
source: 1599, delivered subcutaneously, proved an effective partner agent when combined with rifampin and pyrazinamide and also with bedaquiline, pretomanid, or moxifloxacin in TB mouse efficacy models of increasing complexity (Robertson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Aerosolized administration of spectinamide 1599 has been tested in preclinical in vivo studies using liquid formulation.
source: Aerosolized administration of 1599 has been tested in preclinical in vivo studies using the liquid formulation of the drug.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Inhaled spectinamide 1599, used in monotherapy or in combination with pyrazinamide, is efficacious and well tolerated in murine TB efficacy models.
source: These studies have shown that inhaled 1599, used in monotherapy or in combination with pyrazinamide, is efficacious and well tolerated in murine TB efficacy models (Boisson et al., 2014; Rathi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 showed 48 times higher exposure in mouse lungs via inhalation compared to equivalent dosages administered by subcutaneous injection.
source: A comparative study assessing the biodistribution of the drug in relation to the administration route demonstrated that 1599 showed 48 times higher exposure in mouse lungs via inhalation compared to equivalent dosages administered by subcutaneous injection; the latter may explain the increased efficacy of this drug following intrapulmonary aerosol (Gonzalez-Juarrero et al., 2021; Rathi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 is amenable to dry powder formulation and delivery.
source: Moreover, 1599 was shown to be amenable to dry powder formulation and delivery, suggesting a pathway to a more patient-friendly delivery system (Hickey et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The BALB/c chronic TB model develops homogenous lung granulomatous lesions restraining bacilli within intracellular compartments of macrophages and foamy macrophages.
source: The BALB/c chronic TB model is representative of a long-term Mtb chronic infection that develops homogenous lung granulomatous lesions restraining the bacilli within intracellular compartments (De Groote et al., 2011) of macrophages and foamy macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: C3HeB/FeJ mice infected with Mtb exhibit a heterogenous spectrum of lesions including granulomas and caseous necrotic lesions surrounded by a fibrotic rim.
source: In contrast, low-dose aerosol Mtb infection of C3HeB/FeJ mice also results in a chronic infection, but their lungs exhibit a heterogenous spectrum of lesions including granulomas similar to those seen in BALB/c chronic TB model in addition to caseous necrotic lesions surrounded by a fibrotic rim (Robertson et al., 2021; Irwin et al., 2015; Driver et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The caseum of necrotic granulomas in C3HeB/FeJ mice creates a hypoxic environment and contains abundant extracellular bacilli.
source: The caseum of these necrotic granulomas creates a hypoxic environment and contains abundant extracellular bacilli (Irwin et al., 2015; Driver et al., 2012; Lanoix et al., 2015) in a similar fashion to necrotic granulomas found in some human TB patients.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Treatment of C3HeB/FeJ mice with linezolid for 4 weeks resulted in an average of 0.51 log10 CFU reduction in the lungs compared to untreated control.
source: Treatment of C3HeB/FeJ mice with L (7.30±0.45 log10) or S (6.90±0.48 log10) for 4 weeks resulted in an average of 0.51 and 0.91 log10 CFU reduction in the lungs respectively, compared to untreated (UnRx) control (7.81±0.36 log10) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Treatment of C3HeB/FeJ mice with spectinamide 1599 for 4 weeks resulted in an average of 0.91 log10 CFU reduction in the lungs compared to untreated control.
source: Treatment of C3HeB/FeJ mice with L (7.30±0.45 log10) or S (6.90±0.48 log10) for 4 weeks resulted in an average of 0.51 and 0.91 log10 CFU reduction in the lungs respectively, compared to untreated (UnRx) control (7.81±0.36 log10) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The difference in lung CFU reduction between linezolid and spectinamide 1599 monotherapy in C3HeB/FeJ mice failed to achieve statistical significance.
source: This difference failed to achieve statistical significance owing to the larger standard deviation associated with heterogenous advanced lung pathology observed in this model (Rathi et al., 2019; Irwin et al., 2015; Driver et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Linezolid-treated C3HeB/FeJ mice had significantly lower spleen bacterial burden compared to untreated control.
source: In contrast, L (4.49±0.10 log10) treated C3HeB/FeJ mice had significantly lower spleen bacterial burden compared to UnRx (5.43±0.27 log10), with no significant difference between the L and S (4.94±0.11 log10) treatment arm (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: There was no significant difference in spleen bacterial burden between linezolid and spectinamide 1599 treatment in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: In contrast, L (4.49±0.10 log10) treated C3HeB/FeJ mice had significantly lower spleen bacterial burden compared to UnRx (5.43±0.27 log10), with no significant difference between the L and S (4.94±0.11 log10) treatment arm (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Linezolid or spectinamide 1599 treatment promoted a significant reduction in lung bacterial burden (0.83 and 0.77 log10, respectively) compared to untreated or vehicle-only controls in BALB/c mice.
source: In BALB/c mice, L or S treatment was found to promote a significant reduction in lung bacterial burden (0.83 and 0.77 log10, respectively) compared to UnRx or the vehicle-only controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: There was no significant difference in lung bacterial burden after linezolid or spectinamide 1599 treatment in BALB/c mice.
source: There was no significant difference in lung bacterial burden after L or S treatment in BALB/c mice and there was no change in spleen bacterial burden compared to UnRx control (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: There was no change in spleen bacterial burden after linezolid or spectinamide 1599 treatment compared to untreated control in BALB/c mice.
source: There was no significant difference in lung bacterial burden after L or S treatment in BALB/c mice and there was no change in spleen bacterial burden compared to UnRx control (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Compared to untreated control, mice in the BPa, BPaL and BPaS treatment groups had significantly reduced lung bacterial burden by 1.99, 2.72, and 2.50 log10, respectively in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Compared to UnRx (7.48±0.12 log10) control, mice in the BPa (5.49±0.42 log10), BPaL (4.76±0.38 log10) and BPaS (4.98±0.35 log10) treatment groups had significantly reduced the lung bacterial burden by 1.99, 2.72, and 2.50 log10, respectively (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: The differences in lung CFU reduction between BPaL or BPaS and BPa backbone regimen failed to achieve statistical significance in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Although a higher CFU reduction was observed in the lungs of C3HeB/FeJ mice treated with BPaL or BPaS, these differences failed to achieve statistical significance compared to the BPa backbone regimen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: All three regimens (BPa, BPaL, BPaS) proved highly effective at reducing spleen bacterial burden in C3HeB/FeJ mice, with most mice returning no CFU within the limit of detection.
source: All three regimens proved highly effective at reducing spleen bacterial burden in C3HeB/FeJ mice, with most mice returning no CFU within the limit of detection (LOD) employed herein (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1G.

claim: Compared to untreated control, mice in the BPaL and BPaS treatment groups returned significantly fewer CFU in the lungs of BALB/c mice, with most mice returning no CFU within the limit of detection.
source: The combined result demonstrated that compared to UnRx (5.24±0.17 log10) control, mice in the BPaL (1.29±0.13 log10) and BPaS (1.44±0.17 log10) treatment groups returned significantly fewer CFU in the lungs, with most mice returning no CFU within the LOD employed herein (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: No significant difference was observed in the lung CFU of BALB/c mice treated with either the BPaL or BPaS regimen.
source: As in the C3HeB/FeJ TB model, no significant difference was observed in the lung CFU of BALB/c mice treated with either the BPaL or BPaS regimen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: BPaL and BPaS therapy reduced BALB/c spleen bacterial burden to below the limit of detection with no CFU recovered for any treated mice.
source: BPaL and BPaS therapy reduced BALB/c spleen bacterial burden to below the LOD of the assay with no CFU recovered for any treated mice (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1H.

claim: No significant difference in body weight among treatment groups in C3HeB/FeJ or BALB/c mice was observed following 4 weeks of treatment with spectinamide 1599 or linezolid alone.
source: No significant difference in the body weight among the treatment groups in either C3HeB/FeJ or BALB/c mice was observed following 4 weeks of treatment with S or L alone (Figure 1—figure supplements 4–7 and Figure 1—figure supplements 10–12, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figure supplements.

claim: C3HeB/FeJ or BALB/c mice treated with BPa, BPaL, or BPaS showed marginal loss of body weight, ranging from 2.37–5.13%.
source: On the other hand, C3HeB/FeJ or BALB/c mice treated with BPa, BPaL, or BPaS showed marginal loss of body weight, ranging from 2.37–5.13% and only mice receiving the BPaL regimen, when compared to the UnRx control, reached statistically significant loses in body weight by the end of treatment (Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 10, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figure supplements.

claim: Only mice receiving the BPaL regimen reached statistically significant losses in body weight by the end of treatment when compared to untreated control.
source: On the other hand, C3HeB/FeJ or BALB/c mice treated with BPa, BPaL, or BPaS showed marginal loss of body weight, ranging from 2.37–5.13% and only mice receiving the BPaL regimen, when compared to the UnRx control, reached statistically significant loses in body weight by the end of treatment (Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 10, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figure supplements.

claim: Lung lesions of untreated Mtb-infected C3HeB/FeJ mice showed a spectrum of diverse granuloma types ranging from aggregations of macrophages and lymphocytes to highly organized granulomas with collagen encapsulation and central caseous necrosis.
source: The lesions in Mtb-infected UnRx C3HeB/FeJ mice (Figure 2A and B) showed a spectrum of diverse granuloma types ranging from aggregations of macrophages and lymphocytes to highly organized granulomas with collagen encapsulation and a region of central caseous necrosis that resembles to those found in some human patients (Irwin et al., 2015; Driver et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A and B and citations.

claim: Lung lesions of untreated Mtb-infected BALB/c mice consisted of granulomas with a very homogeneous structure formed by aggregations of macrophages and lymphocytes without a necrotic core.
source: By comparison, lung lesions of Mtb-infected UnRx BALB/c mice (Figure 2C and D) consisted of granulomas with a very homogeneous structure (Irwin et al., 2015) formed also by aggregations of macrophages and lymphocytes without a necrotic core.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C and D and a citation.

claim: Mice treated for 4 weeks with the BPaL or BPaS regimen presented with a significant reduction in the number and size of granulomas in both C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c TB models compared to their respective untreated control.
source: Mice treated for 4 weeks with the BPaL or BPaS regimen presented with a significant reduction in the number and size of granulomas in both C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c TB models compared to their respective UnRx control, with no significant difference in lesion burden score between the combination drug treatment groups (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2E and F.

claim: There was no significant difference in lesion burden score between BPaL and BPaS treatment groups in C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c mice.
source: Mice treated for 4 weeks with the BPaL or BPaS regimen presented with a significant reduction in the number and size of granulomas in both C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c TB models compared to their respective UnRx control, with no significant difference in lesion burden score between the combination drug treatment groups (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2E and F.

claim: Linezolid treatment significantly increased red blood cell distribution width standard deviation (RDWs) compared to untreated control and spectinamide 1599-treated mice in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: When compared to UnRx control and S-treated mice, L treatment significantly increased the red blood cell distribution width standard deviation (RDWs), while both L and S treatment were associated with a significant decrease in the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) compared to UnRx control (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Both linezolid and spectinamide 1599 treatment were associated with a significant decrease in mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) compared to untreated control in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: When compared to UnRx control and S-treated mice, L treatment significantly increased the red blood cell distribution width standard deviation (RDWs), while both L and S treatment were associated with a significant decrease in the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) compared to UnRx control (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: None of the 20 parameters of complete blood count changed during the first 2 weeks of treatment with BPa, BPaL, or BPaS in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: None of the 20 parameters of CBC changed during the first 2 weeks of treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: A total of four blood parameters were affected at 4 weeks of treatment with BPa, BPaL, or BPaS in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: However, out of the 20 blood parameters evaluated, a total of four blood parameters were affected at 4 weeks of treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Linezolid-containing BPaL regimen was associated with a significant increase in RDWs and lower hemoglobin (HGB) compared to untreated control after 4 weeks in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: L-containing BPaL regimen was again associated with a significant increase in the RDWs, and lower hemoglobin (HGB) compared to UnRx control after 4 weeks.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The effects of increased RDWs and lower HGB were not observed in mice treated with BPa or BPaS.
source: This effect was not observed in mice treated with BPa or BPaS (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: There was a trend towards lower overall MCHC in mice treated with either BPaL or BPaS at 4 weeks.
source: However, as in monotherapy, there was a trend towards lower overall MCHC in mice treated with either BPaL or BPaS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Mean platelet volume (MPV) was marginally higher at 4 weeks in mice treated with BPa compared to BPaL or BPaS, albeit not significantly different from untreated control.
source: The mean platelet volume (MPV) was marginally higher at 4 weeks in mice treated with BPa compared to BPaL or BPaS, albeit not significantly different from UnRx control (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The significant HGB decrease and RDWs increase were associated with inclusion of linezolid in the BPaL regimen.
source: Given that no difference in HGB or RDWs was observed between UnRx control and their comparator BPa and BPaS regimens, we concluded that the significant HGB decrease and RDWs increase (often observed during the development of anemia) were associated with inclusion of L in the BPaL regimen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: BPa and BPaL treatment significantly decreased myeloid cells while increasing the proportion of erythroid cells in bone marrow of C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: The BPa and BPaL treatment significantly decreased myeloid cells while increasing the proportion of erythroid cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: The myeloid to erythroid ratio in the bone marrow of animals treated with BPaL or BPa was lower compared to untreated control in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Hence, the corresponding ratio in the bone marrow of animals treated with BPaL or BPa was lower compared to the UnRx control.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: BPaS treatment did not show any difference in the content of myeloid or erythroid cells when compared to untreated control in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Importantly, the BPaS treatment did not show any difference in the content of myeloid or erythroid cells when compared to UnRx control suggesting that S in the BPaS was able to recover this effect.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Spectinamide in the BPaS regimen was able to recover the altered myeloid to erythroid ratio effect observed with BPa and BPaL.
source: Importantly, the BPaS treatment did not show any difference in the content of myeloid or erythroid cells when compared to UnRx control suggesting that S in the BPaS was able to recover this effect.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: No significant difference in myeloid and other cell types was found among control and treatment groups in bone marrow of BALB/c mice.
source: In Mtb-infected BALB/c mice, the number of myeloid and other cell types were counted, however, no significant difference was found among the control and treatment groups (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Bone marrow samples demonstrated appreciably higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in BPaL-treated compared to BPaS-treated C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: The bone marrow samples demonstrated a significant difference between the BPaL and BPaS groups, with appreciably higher level of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines (IL-1β, IL-12p70, IL-23, TNFα, GROα (CXCL1), MP-2α (CXCL2), IP-10 (CXCL10), MP-1α (CCL3), RANTES (CCL5), MCP-3 (CCL7), and Eotaxin (CCL11)) in the BPaL- compared to BPaS-treated mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Plasma and lung samples had similar cytokine and chemokine contents between BPaL and BPaS treatment groups except for MCP-3 (CCL7) in plasma which was significantly higher in BPaS compared to BPaL.
source: The plasma and lung samples, however, had similar cytokine and chemokine contents the treatment groups except for MCP-3 (CCL7) in plasma which was significantly higher in BPaS compared to the BPaL group (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: There was a strong correlation between the profound reduction of lung bacterial burden and the profound reduction in bone marrow cytokine and chemokine contents observed in mice from BPaL or BPaS groups compared to untreated control.
source: The analysis suggested that compared to UnRx control, there was a strong correlation between the profound reduction of lung bacterial burden and the profound reduction in bone marrow cytokine and chemokine contents observed in mice from BPaL or BPaS groups.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from correlation analysis.

claim: Similar correlations were found between lung CFU and content of cytokines and chemokines in lung and plasma.
source: Similar correlations were found between lung CFU and content of cytokines and chemokines in lung (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) and plasma (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figure supplements.

claim: Compared to untreated control, there was a significant decrease in the percentage of inflammatory myeloid phenotypes in bone marrow in response to therapy with either BPa, BPaL, or BPaS in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: The bone marrow (Figure 5A) results revealed that as compared to UnRx control, there was a significant decrease in the percentage of inflammatory myeloid phenotypes (CD45 +CD3-CD11b+CD11c-Ly6C+CCR2+, CD45 +CD3-CD11b+CD11c-Ly6C+CCR2+MHC-II+and CD45+CD3-D14+CCR2+) in response to therapy with either BPa, BPaL, or BPaS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Neutrophils, precursor T cells, and B cells were significantly increased in either BPa, BPaL, or BPaS treatment groups compared to untreated control in bone marrow of C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: In contrast, neutrophils (CD45 +CD3-CD11b+CD11c-Ly6C+Ly6Ghigh), precursor T cells (CD45 +CD3+), and B cells (CD45 +CD3 CD19+B220-) were significantly increased in either BPa, BPaL, or BPaS treatment groups compared to UnRx control in bone marrow.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The reduced inflammatory response in treatment groups is consistent in blood shown by significantly reduced inflammatory myeloid cells in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: This reduced inflammatory response in treatment groups is also consistent in blood shown by significantly reduced inflammatory myeloid cells (CD45 +CD3-CD11b+CD11c-Ly6C+CCR2+) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: The response to therapy in the lungs was manifested by a significant increase of CD3+CD4+ T helper cells and B-1 cells in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Interestingly, the response to therapy in the lungs (Figure 5C) was manifested by a significant increase of CD3 +CD4+T helper cells and B-1 cells (CD3-CD19+) and a reverse trend for CD3 +CD8+and γδ-T cells (CD3 +CD8+γδTCR+).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: There was a reverse trend for CD3+CD8+ and γδ-T cells in the lungs in response to therapy in C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Interestingly, the response to therapy in the lungs (Figure 5C) was manifested by a significant increase of CD3 +CD4+T helper cells and B-1 cells (CD3-CD19+) and a reverse trend for CD3 +CD8+and γδ-T cells (CD3 +CD8+γδTCR+).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: BPaL and BPaS treatments significantly and dramatically lowered the number of neutrophils (Ly6G+) compared to untreated control in lungs of C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: The analysis of mfIHC images revealed that the BPaL and BPaS treatments significantly and dramatically lowered the number of neutrophils (count based on Ly6G+) compared to UnRx control, however, F4/80+ cells were observed significantly higher in BPaS compared to UnRx control (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: F4/80+ cells were observed significantly higher in BPaS compared to untreated control in lungs of C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: The analysis of mfIHC images revealed that the BPaL and BPaS treatments significantly and dramatically lowered the number of neutrophils (count based on Ly6G+) compared to UnRx control, however, F4/80+ cells were observed significantly higher in BPaS compared to UnRx control (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: A significant decrease in neutrophils was positively correlated with the corresponding increase in most of the other immune cells in lungs of C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Interestingly, the spearman's correlation plot (Figure 6D) shows that a significant decrease in neutrophils was positively correlated with the corresponding increase in most of the other immune cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: Both BPaL and BPaS multidrug regimens significantly reduced lung bacterial burden by 3.8–4.0 log10 and 2.5–2.7 log10 in BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ TB models, respectively.
source: Both multidrug regimens such as BPaL or BPaS significantly reduced lung bacterial burden by 3.8–4.0 log10 and 2.5–2.7 log10 in BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ TB models, respectively (Figure 1E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to figures.

claim: Both BPaL and BPaS regimens promote similar bactericidal effects in murine models lacking or featuring advanced pulmonary pathology.
source: We, therefore, conclude that both regimens promote similar bactericidal effects in murine models lacking, or featuring, advanced pulmonary pathology.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion.

claim: The potent antimicrobial effect of the BPaL and BPaS regimens resulted in improvement of the pathological outcome during chronic infection with Mtb.
source: Furthermore, the potent antimicrobial effect of the BPaL and BPaS regimens also resulted in improvement of the pathological outcome during chronic infection with Mtb but only the L-containing BPaL regimen, not BPaS, was associated with a significant decrease in the body weight at week 4 in Mtb-infected BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice (Figure 4; Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 10).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with references to figures.

claim: Only the linezolid-containing BPaL regimen, not BPaS, was associated with a significant decrease in body weight at week 4 in Mtb-infected BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Furthermore, the potent antimicrobial effect of the BPaL and BPaS regimens also resulted in improvement of the pathological outcome during chronic infection with Mtb but only the L-containing BPaL regimen, not BPaS, was associated with a significant decrease in the body weight at week 4 in Mtb-infected BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice (Figure 4; Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 10).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with references to figures.

claim: The extent of weight loss is an important preclinical and clinical parameter in TB patients because it determines the severity of disease progression.
source: The extent of weight loss is an important preclinical and clinical parameter in TB patients because it determines the severity of disease progression (van Crevel et al., 2002), and it is also an indicator of in vivo drug efficacy (Nikonenko et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Weight loss is an indicator of in vivo drug efficacy.
source: The extent of weight loss is an important preclinical and clinical parameter in TB patients because it determines the severity of disease progression (van Crevel et al., 2002), and it is also an indicator of in vivo drug efficacy (Nikonenko et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: The incidence of anemia is reported up to 62.5% in MDR and XDR-TB patients.
source: Among L-associated hematological side effects, the incidence of anemia is reported up to 62.5% in MDR and XDR-TB patients (Dayyab et al., 2021; Palomino and Martin, 2014; Sotgiu et al., 2012) and the onset of this effect can occur at 2 weeks to 2 months of L administration (Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: The onset of anemia can occur at 2 weeks to 2 months of linezolid administration.
source: Among L-associated hematological side effects, the incidence of anemia is reported up to 62.5% in MDR and XDR-TB patients (Dayyab et al., 2021; Palomino and Martin, 2014; Sotgiu et al., 2012) and the onset of this effect can occur at 2 weeks to 2 months of L administration (Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: In TB patients treated with anti-TB drugs, increased RDWs and lower HGB are associated with anemia and serve as markers of disease prognosis.
source: In TB patients treated with anti-TB drugs (Mirlohi et al., 2016; Kassa et al., 2016; Luo et al., 2022), increased RDWs and lower HGB are associated with anemia and these parameters serve as markers of disease prognosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Mild hematological effects observed in mice treated for 4 weeks with linezolid or BPaL are dependent on the number of linezolid doses administered and are time-dependent.
source: This is interpreted to mean that mild hematological effects observed in mice treated for 4 weeks with L or BPaL are dependent on the number of L-doses administered and are thus, time-dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The onset of hematological effects when testing a linezolid-containing regimen (BPaL) is in agreement with previous studies in human patients.
source: Overall, the onset of these hematological effects when testing an L-containing regimen (BPaL) is in agreement with previous studies (Tang et al., 2015; Gerson et al., 2002) in human patients.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: The mechanism of linezolid-induced toxicity is attributed to its binding with host mitochondrial ribosomes leading to mitochondrial toxicities.
source: The mechanism of L-induced toxicity is attributed to its binding with the host mitochondrial ribosomes leading to mitochondrial toxicities (De Vriese et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Linezolid binding to mitochondrial ribosomes results in activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome.
source: The latter results in the activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome (Iyer et al., 2013) and subsequently results in L-mediated bone marrow myelosuppression Winchell et al., 2020; a phenomenon consistent with the hematologic anomalies seen in patients treated with L for extended time periods.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Linezolid-mediated activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome results in bone marrow myelosuppression.
source: The latter results in the activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome (Iyer et al., 2013) and subsequently results in L-mediated bone marrow myelosuppression Winchell et al., 2020; a phenomenon consistent with the hematologic anomalies seen in patients treated with L for extended time periods.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Because spectinamides do not bind to mitochondrial ribosomes there is reduced potential for similar side effects.
source: Because spectinamides do not bind to mitochondrial ribosomes there is reduced potential for similar side effects (Lee et al., 2014; Modongo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Myeloid to erythroid ratio (M:E) provides information about the relative proportions of myeloid lineage to erythroid lineage.
source: To conclusively test this hypothesis, we performed bone marrow histopathology to quantify the myeloid to erythroid ratio (M:E), a parameter that provides information about the relative proportions of myeloid lineage (granulocytes, monocytes, and their precursors) to erythroid lineage (Elmore, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Linezolid was previously shown to impact myeloid to erythroid ratio, although an opposite trend was observed in studies employing 12 days of linezolid administration in a different strain of otherwise healthy mice.
source: L was previously shown to impact M:E ratio, although an opposite trend was observed in those studies, which employed 12- days of L administration and a different strain of otherwise healthy mice (Iyer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Elevation of interleukin 1β (IL-1β) levels and activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome have been previously linked to myelosuppression.
source: Elevation of interleukin 1β (IL-1β) levels and activation of Nlrp3 inflammasome have been previously linked to myelosuppression (Winchell et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: The presence of elevated IL-1β was previously reported during monotherapy with linezolid.
source: The presence of elevated IL-1β was previously reported during monotherapy with L (Iyer et al., 2013; Jasenosky et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: The favorable treatment outcomes may promote a corresponding decline in the Ly6G neutrophil population.
source: An implication of this finding is that the favorable treatment outcomes may promote a corresponding decline in the Ly6G neutrophil population as suggested before (Lovewell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Among all immune cell phenotypes studied, no differences were found between BPaL and BPaS treated animals.
source: Among all immune cell phenotypes studied, no differences were found between BPaL and BPaS treated animals, and only the F4/80+ cells in the BPaS (but not in the BPaL) treated animals showed a significant increase when compared to the UnRx control.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Only F4/80+ cells in the BPaS (but not in the BPaL) treated animals showed a significant increase when compared to untreated control.
source: Among all immune cell phenotypes studied, no differences were found between BPaL and BPaS treated animals, and only the F4/80+ cells in the BPaS (but not in the BPaL) treated animals showed a significant increase when compared to the UnRx control.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The human use of spectinamides 1599 will be administered using a dry powder formulation delivered by the RS01 Plastiape dry powder inhaler.
source: It is proposed that the human use of spectinamides 1599 will be administered using a dry powder formulation delivered by the RS01 Plastiape dry powder inhaler.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The aerodynamic properties of dry powder spectinamide 1599 within #3 HPMC capsules delivered from a RS01 Plastiape inhaler device have been reported.
source: We already reported on the aerodynamic properties of dry powder spectinamide 1599 within #3 HPMC capsules and delivered from a RS01 Plastiape inhaler device (Stewart et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Female C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c mice at 6–8 weeks of age were purchased from the Jackson Laboratories.
source: Female C3HeB/FeJ and BALB/c mice at 6–8 weeks of age were purchased from the Jackson Laboratories.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Animals were infected with a low-dose aerosol infection of Mtb (Erdman strain; ATCC 35801) using an inhalation exposure system calibrated to deliver ~50–100 colony-forming units (CFU) to the lungs.
source: Animals were infected with a low-dose aerosol infection of Mtb (Erdman strain; ATCC 35801) using an inhalation exposure system (Glas-Col, Terre Haute, IN) calibrated to deliver ~50–100 colony-forming units (CFU) to the lungs (Gonzalez-Juarrero et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: Bedaquiline was administered at 25 mg/kg.
source: B was administered at 25 mg/kg.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Pretomanid and linezolid were administered at 100 mg/kg each.
source: Pa and L were administered at 100 mg/kg each and S was delivered by inhalation in liquid form at 50 and 100 mg/kg to BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Spectinamide 1599 was delivered by inhalation in liquid form at 50 and 100 mg/kg to BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice, respectively.
source: Pa and L were administered at 100 mg/kg each and S was delivered by inhalation in liquid form at 50 and 100 mg/kg to BALB/c and C3HeB/FeJ mice, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Drug treatment was started 4 weeks post-aerosol infection for BALB/c and at 8–9 weeks post-aerosol infection for C3HeB/FeJ mice.
source: Drug treatment was started 4 weeks post-aerosol infection for BALB/c and at 8–9 weeks post-aerosol infection for C3HeB/FeJ mice to allow time for lung pathology to fully develop.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: All drugs were administered once daily for 5 days/week for 4 weeks by oral (gavage) administration except spectinamide 1599 which was administered 3 days/week by intrapulmonary aerosol delivery.
source: All drugs were administered once daily for 5 days/week for 4 weeks by oral (gavage) administration except S which was administered 3 days/week by intrapulmonary aerosol delivery using the Penn Century microsprayer as reported previously (Gonzalez-Juarrero et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.
